Section I: Program Overview & Background 1.1 Purpose The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Directorate, AFLCMC/GBGD, is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify and acquire an innovative, commercially available Digital Adoption Platform (DAP). This platform will replace the legacy Oracle User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready so

User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready software-guided training and performance-support tool. It must streamline content creation, simplify software adoption, and provide real-time in-application guidance for the DEAMS user base. 1.2 Mission Impact & Capability Gap The current solution (Oracle UPK) represents unsupported software and significant technical debt. Its retirement creates a critical operational gap in how training is conducted across the enterprise. The replacement DAP will modernize training material outputs, provide interactive in-application assistance, and reduce the overall training footprint. This capability is designated as a Criticality (1) — Must Have requirement to support continuous financial and enterprise operations. 1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to

1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to Production. 2. Section II: Areas of Interest (AOIs) The Air Force is seeking commercial solutions that address three primary Areas of Interest (AOIs). Proposals will be evaluated on how comprehensively they meet the validated requirements within each AOI: 2.1 AOI 1: Content Authoring & Development • No-Code Content Creation: The solution must provide an intuitive, user-friendly authoring interface that allows non-technical personnel to rapidly record, create, and update application guidance without writing code. • Multi-Format Recording: Authors must have the ability to record user interactions with web-based applications (specifically Oracle EBS) and desktop applications to automatically generate simulations, step-by-step instructions, and videos. Addendum to RFO 52.212-2 – Evaluation Procedures and Criteria for Selecting Proposals GBG will utilize a two-step evaluation process. In step 1, Oﬀerors submit a cover letter, ROM, white papers and an eligibility checklist. In step 2, Oﬀerors will submit a proposal and present a live pitch virtually or in-person to the GBG team. After receipt of step 1 proposals, the Air Force will conduct an evaluation based on three factors: technical, importance to agency programs, and funds availability. • The technical factor will assess how innovative the solution is (as deﬁned in this announcement) and the feasibility of the solution solving the unit’s challenges. • The importance to agency programs factor will assess the solution’s potential to enhance the mission eﬀectiveness of the unit. • The funds availability factor will assess the availability of funding to purchase the solution at Pitch Day. Price shall be considered to the extent appropriate, but at a minimum, to determine that the price is fair and reasonable. As such, ensure that the total price is included in your proposal.
